stories.summary: Implement Native Video Compression (Post-Expo Go)
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a User, I want my videos compressed before upload so that uploads are faster and don't crash the AI service.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
DM-29 added video compression infrastructure, but actual compression is disabled in Expo Go due to native module limitations.

Current State:
- VideoCompressionService exists with proper API
- UI for compression progress implemented
- Service currently skips compression and returns original file
- Works in Expo Go for development

Target State:
- Compress videos to 720p @ 2.5 Mbps before upload
- Reduce file sizes from 50-100MB to 10-20MB
- Prevent AI service crashes (512MB RAM limit)
- Improve upload speed and data usage

This is a duplicate of DM-58, created earlier.

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* Replace stub compression in VideoCompressionService with real FFmpeg or native compression
* Compress videos to 720p (1280px width) with 2.5 Mbps bitrate
* Skip compression for files already < 10MB
* Show accurate progress during compression (0-100%)
* Handle compression failures gracefully (fallback to original)
* Test on iOS and Android physical devices
* Verify compressed videos upload successfully
* Verify AI service processes compressed videos without crashes
* Measure compression time (target: < 10s for 30s video)
* Measure file size reduction (target: 70-80% reduction)

h3. ⚙️ Technical Implementation Details
* See DM-58 for full implementation details
* 
* This ticket is a duplicate - close in favor of DM-58

h3. ⚠️ Edge Cases & Constraints

stories.summary: Serve Videos via HTTP Endpoint
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a Developer, I want videos to be accessible via HTTP URLs so that the mobile app can stream them directly.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
Currently, video_url in the database stores local file paths like `/backend/uploads/video.mp4`. These cannot be opened by the mobile app using Linking.openURL() or streamed in a video player.

We need to either:
1. Serve videos via a FastAPI static file endpoint
2. Upload videos to cloud storage (S3, Supabase Storage) and store HTTP URLs

Option 1 is simpler for MVP, Option 2 is better for production scale.

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* Videos accessible via HTTP URL (e.g., https://backend.com/videos/{filename})
* Support video streaming (range requests for seeking)
* CORS headers configured for mobile app access
* Proper content-type headers (video/mp4)
* Authentication/authorization for video access (optional)
* Update video_url in database to store full HTTP URLs

h3. ⚙️ Technical Implementation Details
* Option 1: FastAPI Static Files (Recommended for MVP)
* ```python
* from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
* app.mount('/videos', StaticFiles(directory='uploads'), name='videos')
* ```
* 
* Option 2: Cloud Storage (Production)
* - Use Supabase Storage or AWS S3
* - Upload videos during /upload endpoint
* - Store public URL in video_url column
* 
* Implementation Steps:
* 1. Add static file mount for /videos endpoint
* 2. Update upload endpoint to store full URL
* 3. Add CORS headers for video streaming
* 4. Test range requests for video seeking
* 
* Migration:
* - Update existing video_url records to full URLs
* - Script: `UPDATE swings SET video_url = CONCAT('https://backend.com', video_url)`

h3. ⚠️ Edge Cases & Constraints
* Large video files - ensure streaming works (range requests)
* Concurrent video access - check server capacity
* Video file permissions - ensure readable by web server
* HTTPS required for mobile apps - configure SSL
* Video deleted but URL still in DB - return 404 gracefully

stories.summary: Frame-by-Frame Video Scrubbing
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a User, I want to scrub through my swing video frame-by-frame so that I can analyze specific moments in detail.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
Currently, users can only play/pause the video. For detailed analysis, they need the ability to:
- Scrub through the video using a slider
- Step forward/backward one frame at a time
- See the skeleton overlay update in sync with the current frame

This feature enables coaches and players to examine critical moments like contact point, follow-through, and specific mechanical flaws.

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* Add a slider component below the video player
* Slider syncs with current video playback position
* Dragging slider updates video position and skeleton overlay
* Add step forward button (advance 1 frame)
* Add step backward button (go back 1 frame)
* Skeleton overlay updates to match current frame
* Display current frame number and timestamp
* Works in both normal and fullscreen modes
* Smooth scrubbing performance (no lag)

h3. ⚙️ Technical Implementation Details
* Use expo-video player API for frame-level control
* Calculate frame index from current playback time
* Update skeleton overlay based on frame index
* Add Slider component from React Native
* Add step buttons with ChevronLeft/ChevronRight icons
* 
* Implementation:
* - Get current playback time from player.currentTime
* - Calculate frame index: Math.floor(currentTime * fps)
* - Seek to specific frame: player.currentTime = frameIndex / fps
* - Update skeleton overlay when frame changes
* 
* UI Layout:
* - Slider below video (full width)
* - Step buttons on either side of slider
* - Frame counter display (e.g., 'Frame 45 / 900')
* - Timestamp display (e.g., '1.5s / 30.0s')

h3. ⚠️ Edge Cases & Constraints
* Video not loaded - disable scrubbing controls
* No analysis data - show video only, no skeleton
* Scrubbing while video is playing - pause first
* Rapid scrubbing - debounce skeleton updates
* Frame boundaries - clamp to valid range [0, totalFrames-1]
* Different frame rates - calculate correctly for 30fps, 60fps, etc.

Target State:

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* Replace stub compression in VideoCompressionService with real FFmpeg or native compression
* Compress videos to 720p (1280px width) with 2.5 Mbps bitrate
* Skip compression for files already < 10MB
* Show accurate progress during compression (0-100%)

h3. ⚙️ Technical Implementation Details

* - expo-av with FFmpeg (recommended for Expo)
* - react-native-compressor (requires custom dev client)

stories.summary: Swing History Enhancements: View, Edit, and Delete
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a user, I want to view, edit, and delete my swing history so that I can manage my swing library effectively and add context to help me remember each swing.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
Currently, users can see a list of their swings in the Profile screen, but:

- Swing filenames are random strings (e.g., 'video_1234567890.mp4')

- Users cannot delete old swings

* User can add/edit a custom title or notes for each swing
* User can delete a swing from their history

* Delete action requires confirmation to prevent accidental deletion

h3. ⚙️ Technical Implementation Details

* Mobile App Changes:
* 1. View Swing Analysis:
*    - Create SwingDetailScreen.js to display analysis
*    - Load video from swing.video_url
*    - Display skeletal overlay and bat trail
*    - Show attack angle and other metrics
*    - Add 'Edit' and 'Delete' buttons
* 
* 2. Edit Swing Details:
*    - Add modal/screen to edit title and notes
*    - Call PATCH /api/swings/{swing_id} to save changes
*    - Update local state after successful save
*    - Show loading indicator during save
* 
* 3. Delete Swing:
*    - Show confirmation alert before deleting

stories.summary: Add Upload Cleanup for Aborted/Failed Swing Analysis
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a developer, I want proper cleanup of database records when users abort uploads or when AI processing fails, so that we don't accumulate orphaned data in the database.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
Currently, when a user uploads a swing video, the backend creates a Swing record in the database and starts AI processing. If the user cancels the upload or if processing fails, the database records may remain orphaned with no analysis results or incomplete data. This can lead to database bloat and confusion when viewing swing history.

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* Add 'status' field to Swing model (pending, processing, completed, failed)
* Update backend to set status='processing' when upload starts
* Update backend to set status='completed' when analysis finishes successfully
* Update backend to set status='failed' if AI processing errors
* Add cleanup endpoint or scheduled job to remove old 'pending' or 'failed' swings
* Mobile app calls cleanup endpoint when user cancels upload (optional)
* Swing history only shows swings with status='completed'
* Add database migration for new status field

h3. ⚙️ Technical Implementation Details
* Database Schema Changes:
* - Add 'status' ENUM column to swings table: ('pending', 'processing', 'completed', 'failed')
* - Add 'error_message' TEXT column to swings table (nullable)
* - Add index on status for efficient queries
* 
* Backend Changes (main.py):
* - Update POST /api/videos/upload to set status='processing' when creating Swing
* - Update background processor to set status='completed' on success
* - Update background processor to set status='failed' and store error_message on failure
* - Add GET /api/users/{user_id}/swings to filter by status='completed'
* 
* Cleanup Options:
* Option 1: Scheduled Job (Recommended)
* - Add background task that runs every hour
* - Delete swings where status='pending' or 'processing' and created_at > 24 hours ago
* - Delete swings where status='failed' and created_at > 7 days ago
* 
* Option 2: Manual Cleanup Endpoint
* - Add DELETE /api/swings/{swing_id} endpoint
* - Mobile app calls this when user cancels upload
* - Requires tracking swing_id before analysis completes
* 
* Option 3: Transaction-Based (Most Robust)
* - Wrap entire upload + AI processing in a database transaction
* - Only commit when analysis completes successfully
* - Rollback on error or timeout
* - Requires connection pooling adjustments
* 
* Migration Script:
* - Alembic migration to add status and error_message columns
* - Set existing swings to status='completed' (assume they're valid)
* - Add NOT NULL constraint after backfilling

h3. ⚠️ Edge Cases & Constraints
* User cancels upload mid-processing: Backend continues, marks as completed or failed based on AI result
* AI service crashes during processing: Swing remains in 'processing' state, cleanup job removes after 24 hours
* Network timeout between backend and AI service: Backend should catch timeout and set status='failed'
* User uploads same video twice: Both swings are created, both complete successfully (no deduplication needed)
* Cleanup job runs while processing: Only remove swings older than threshold (e.g., 24 hours)
* Database migration on production: Existing swings without status should default to 'completed'
* Concurrent cleanup and status update: Use database locks or WHERE status='pending' in DELETE query

stories.summary: Create Annotated Dataset for YOLO Bat Detection Model
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a Machine Learning Engineer, I want to create a high-quality annotated dataset of baseball bats in swing videos, so that I can train a YOLO object detection model to accurately track bats across various conditions and bat types.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
The current color-based HSV tracking (DM-33) works as a proof-of-concept but has limitations with wood bats, varying lighting, and background noise. To achieve production-grade bat tracking, we need to train a custom YOLO model using a properly annotated dataset of baseball swing videos. This ticket outlines the complete strategy for dataset creation, annotation, and quality assurance.

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* Minimum 500 annotated images (recommended 1000+) of baseball bats in various swing positions
* Dataset includes diversity: aluminum bats (black, red, blue, silver), wood bats, different lighting conditions, indoor/outdoor
* Bounding box annotations in YOLO format (class x_center y_center width height, normalized 0-1)
* Dataset split: 70% training, 20% validation, 10% testing
* Annotation quality validated (no missing bats, accurate bounding boxes, consistent labeling)
* Dataset organized in standard YOLO directory structure with data.yaml configuration
* Documentation of annotation guidelines and dataset statistics

h3. ⚙️ Technical Implementation Details
* **Phase 1: Video Collection & Frame Extraction**
* - Collect 20-30 baseball swing videos (10-60 seconds each)
* - Sources: YouTube (creative commons), personal recordings, stock footage
* - Extract frames at 5 FPS (every 6th frame from 30fps video) to get ~1000-1500 candidate frames
* - Use FFmpeg: `ffmpeg -i swing.mp4 -vf fps=5 frames/frame_%04d.jpg`
* 
* **Phase 2: Frame Selection & Curation**
* - Review extracted frames and select 500-1000 frames with clear bat visibility
* - Prioritize frames showing:
*   - Different swing phases (setup, load, swing, follow-through)
*   - Various bat angles and positions
*   - Challenging scenarios (motion blur, partial occlusion, background clutter)
* - Exclude frames where bat is completely hidden or out of frame
* 
* **Phase 3: Annotation Strategy**
* - Use annotation tool: Roboflow (recommended), LabelImg, or CVAT
* - Create single class: 'bat'
* - Bounding box guidelines:
*   - Box should tightly fit the entire visible bat (from knob to barrel)
*   - Include the bat even if partially occluded by hands
*   - For motion blur, box the blurred region
*   - Minimum box size: 20x20 pixels (avoid tiny/unclear bats)
* - Annotation consistency:
*   - Same annotator for entire dataset (or max 2-3 with clear guidelines)
*   - Review and correct annotations in batches of 100
* 
* **Phase 4: Dataset Organization (YOLO Format)**
* - Directory structure:
*   ```
*   dataset/
*     train/
*       images/
*       labels/
*     val/
*       images/
*       labels/
*     test/
*       images/
*       labels/
*     data.yaml
*   ```
* - Label format (one .txt per image):
*   ```
*   0 0.512 0.384 0.156 0.423
*   # class x_center y_center width height (normalized 0-1)
*   ```
* - data.yaml configuration:
*   ```yaml
*   train: ../train/images
*   val: ../val/images
*   test: ../test/images
*   nc: 1  # number of classes
*   names: ['bat']
*   ```
* 
* **Phase 5: Quality Assurance**
* - Automated validation:
*   - Check all images have corresponding label files
*   - Verify bounding box coordinates are within [0, 1] range
*   - Ensure no empty label files (frames with no bat should be excluded)
* - Manual review:
*   - Sample 10% of annotations for spot-checking
*   - Visualize bounding boxes on images to verify accuracy
*   - Check for consistent box sizing across similar frames
* 
* **Phase 6: Dataset Augmentation (Optional)**
* - Use Roboflow or Albumentations for augmentation:
*   - Horizontal flip (50% probability)
*   - Brightness adjustment (Â±15%)
*   - Slight rotation (Â±5 degrees)
*   - Mosaic augmentation (YOLO-specific)
* - Augmentation can 2-3x effective dataset size
* 
* **Recommended Tools:**
* - **Roboflow** (easiest, has YOLO export, augmentation, and hosting)
* - **LabelImg** (free, desktop app, simple bounding boxes)
* - **CVAT** (advanced, supports collaboration, self-hosted or cloud)
* - **FFmpeg** (video frame extraction)
* - **Python script** (automated dataset splitting and validation)

h3. ⚠️ Edge Cases & Constraints
* **Motion Blur**: Annotate the blurred region as best estimate of bat position. YOLO can learn to handle blur if trained on it.
* **Partial Occlusion**: If >50% of bat is visible, annotate it. If <50%, consider excluding the frame.
* **Multiple Bats in Frame**: Unlikely in swing videos, but annotate all visible bats if present.
* **Bat vs Background Confusion**: Include challenging frames (bat against fence, similar-colored backgrounds) to improve model robustness.
* **Different Camera Angles**: Collect videos from multiple angles (side view, front view, angled) for better generalization.
* **Lighting Variations**: Include indoor (artificial light), outdoor (daylight), and low-light scenarios.
* **Bat Types**: Ensure dataset has ~60% aluminum, ~30% wood, ~10% composite/hybrid bats to match real-world distribution.

stories.summary: Add Toggle Control for Skeleton Overlay Visibility
stories.description:
{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
*User Story*

As a user, I want to toggle the skeleton overlay on and off during video playback, so I can choose whether to view the pose analysis or just the raw video.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal

Currently, the skeleton overlay is always visible when analysis results are available. Users may want to compare their swing with and without the overlay, or simply prefer viewing the raw video without visual annotations.

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)

* A toggle button/switch is visible in the UI when analysis results are loaded.
* Clicking the toggle hides/shows the skeleton overlay without affecting video playback.
* Toggle state persists during video scrubbing and seeking.
* Overlay visibility preference is maintained when switching between analyzed videos in the same session.
* Toggle is disabled or hidden when no analysis results are available.

h3. ⚙️ Technical Implementation Details

* Add a boolean state variable (e.g., `showOverlay`) in App.js.
* Conditionally render the SkeletonOverlay component based on this state.
* Add a toggle button (likely near playback controls) that updates the state.
* Ensure the toggle doesn't trigger unnecessary re-renders of the video player

h3. ⚠️ Edge Cases & Constraints

* Toggle should be disabled during video upload/processing (no results yet).
* Switching videos should reset or maintain toggle state (decide on UX preference).
* Toggle state should not interfere with overlay synchronization logic.
* Consider accessibility: toggle should have proper ARIA labels for screen readers.

stories.summary: Develop AI Coaching Chatbot Interface
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a User, I want to ask follow-up questions to an AI Coach about my analysis via a chat interface in the app.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
Users may not understand the static analysis. A chatbot allows them to ask 'How do I fix this?' or 'What drill should I do?'.

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* Create a new `ChatOverlay` or screen in the Mobile App.
* Implement a chat input that sends user text + current `job_id` context to the backend.
* Backend maintains a short-term conversation history buffer.
* Display streaming responses from the AI Coach.

h3. ⚙️ Technical Implementation Details
* Frontend: React Native Gifted Chat or custom UI.
* Backend: New WebSocket endpoint or HTTP POST for chat messages.
* The backend must inject the current swing's RAG context into the system prompt so the chatbot 'knows' what video is being discussed.

h3. ⚠️ Edge Cases & Constraints
* User asks about non-baseball topics (guardrails needed).
* Network disconnects during streaming response.

stories.summary: Generate LLM Summaries for Swing Comparisons
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a User, I want a text summary explaining *why* my swing was matched with a specific Pro player, so I understand the similarity.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
Semantic search gives us the video, but this story provides the 'Why'. The LLM will compare the data points of the user's swing vs. the retrieved result.

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* Pass the user's swing metrics and the retrieved 'Pro Comp' metrics to the LLM.
* Engineer a prompt to ask for a 'Compare and Contrast' summary (e.g., 'Both you and Judge have a high hand set, but you drift forward earlier').
* Return this summary field in the API response.

h3. ⚙️ Technical Implementation Details
* This extends the RAG pipeline.
* It requires structured context injection (formatting both sets of landmarks into a token-efficient text representation for the LLM).

h3. ⚠️ Edge Cases & Constraints
* Token limit errors if trying to pass raw data for every frame.
* Need to summarize the swing into keyframes (stance, load, contact, follow-through) before sending to LLM.

stories.summary: Implement Semantic Search for Similar Swing Retrieval
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a User, I want to see 'Pro Comps' or past swings that look similar to my current swing, so that I can visually compare my form.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
Using the Vector DB established in the previous story, we will query for 'nearest neighbors' to the user's current swing vector to find similar examples.

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* Create a backend endpoint `/api/swings/search` that accepts a swing ID.
* Implement vector similarity search (Cosine Similarity) to find the top 3 closest matches.
* Return the video URLs and IDs of the matching swings.
* Filter results to ensure diverse comparisons (e.g., matching against a Pro dataset vs. User's history).

h3. ⚙️ Technical Implementation Details
* The search logic resides in the Backend.
* It requests the vector for the target swing from the DB, then runs the similarity query.
* Requires a pre-populated 'Pro Swing' dataset in the DB for effective day-one usage.

h3. ⚠️ Edge Cases & Constraints
* No similar swings found (threshold too strict).
* Finding the user's *own* duplicate uploads as the top match (need to filter out current ID).

stories.summary: Implement RAG Pipeline for Natural Language Swing Analysis
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a Coach, I want the system to generate analysis in natural language based on established baseball coaching knowledge, so that the feedback feels professional and authoritative.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
Instead of just returning raw coordinates, we want the system to explain *what* is wrong using RAG. The system should retrieve relevant coaching tips based on detected flaws (e.g., 'casting', 'early extension').

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* Ingest a baseline dataset of baseball coaching manuals/text into the Vector DB.
* Create a retrieval chain in the Backend that queries the DB based on specific pose error signatures.
* Integrate an LLM (e.g., OpenAI/Anthropic) to synthesize the retrieved context into a cohesive critique.
* Return a string of natural language text alongside the existing JSON pose data.

h3. ⚙️ Technical Implementation Details
* Use LangChain or basic OpenAI API calls in `backend`.
* Requires a new Env Var for LLM API Keys.
* The 'query' to the RAG system will be constructed from the specific deviations found in the MediaPipe landmarks.

h3. ⚠️ Edge Cases & Constraints
* Hallucinations where the LLM invents coaching terms.
* RAG retrieving irrelevant advice if the swing flaw is ambiguous.

stories.summary: Integrate Vector Database for Swing Persistence
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a Developer, I want to store swing analysis data (pose landmarks) in a Vector Database (Pinecone or Weaviate) so that I can perform semantic searches and retrieval later.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
Currently, swing data is ephemeral. To enable RAG and comparison features, we need persistent storage optimized for similarity search. This serves as the foundational infrastructure for the upcoming GenAI features.

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* Provision a Vector Database instance (Pinecone or Weaviate) accessible by the Backend and AI Service.
* Define a schema/index for storing flattened pose landmark arrays (33 landmarks * 4 attributes) as embeddings.
* Update `ai-service` to upsert processed swing data to the Vector DB after successful MediaPipe extraction.
* Ensure metadata (User ID, Video ID, Timestamp) is stored alongside the vectors.

h3. ⚙️ Technical Implementation Details
* Install python client for chosen DB in `backend` and `ai-service`.
* Create a new service module `vector_store.py` to handle connection strings (managed via Env Vars).
* Landmarks (x, y, z, visibility) might need normalization before vectorization.

h3. ⚠️ Edge Cases & Constraints
* Handling network timeouts when upserting large batches of historical swings.
* Ensuring vector dimensions match the embedding model limits.

stories.summary: UI/UX: Modernize Home Screen & Unify Error Handling
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a User, I want a professional, modern interface that clearly communicates status without redundant error messages, so that I feel confident using the tool.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
Current UI is raw/MVP. Error messages appear in two places (top and bottom) due to overlapping logic. The styling lacks the 'Sports Tech' aesthetic.

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* Remove the top 'Timeout' icon and text container completely.
* Refine the bottom error toast to look like a modern UI notification (rounded, better font).
* Style the 'Select Swing' area as a modern Card with shadow and distinct button.
* Update typography to use system weights (Bold Headers) for better hierarchy.
* Ensure 'Cold Start' timeouts still trigger the bottom notification.

h3. ⚙️ Technical Implementation Details
* Modify 'App.js' (or main screen component).
* Consolidate state variables for error handling (remove redundant state).
* Use React Native 'StyleSheet' for shadows and rounded corners.
* Keep existing 'UploadService.js' integration intact.

h3. ⚠️ Edge Cases & Constraints
* Ensure the new Error Toast floats above other UI elements (z-index).
* Ensure the UI remains responsive on smaller screens (iPhone SE size).

stories.summary: Optimization: Centralize and Parameterize API URLs
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a Developer, I want to centralize API URLs in a config file (Mobile) and Environment Variables (AI Service) so that I don't have to hunt down hardcoded strings when the backend URL changes.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
We recently experienced a regression where App.js pointed to an old backend (vg35) while UploadService pointed to the new one (yalf).

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* Mobile App reads API_URL and WS_URL from a single src/config.js file.
* AI Service reads BACKEND_URL from os.environ, with a fallback default.
* System functions identically to before (upload, overlay, progress bar).

h3. ⚙️ Technical Implementation Details
* Create diamondmind-mobile/src/config.js
* Refactor UploadService.js and App.js to import from config.js
* Update pose_engine.py to use os.environ.get('BACKEND_URL')

stories.summary: Feature: Export and Download Video with Skeleton Overlay
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a User, I want to download the analyzed video with the green skeleton overlay burned in so that I can share it with my coach or post it to social media.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
The overlay is currently rendered in real-time as an SVG. Exporting requires merging the video stream with the SVG coordinate layer into a single file.

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* Add a 'Download Analysis' button to the results card and fullscreen view.
* Merge VideoView content with SkeletonOverlay into a new MP4.
* Save the resulting file to the device's Media Library or Files app.
* Provide a native Share Sheet after successful export.

stories.summary: Feature: Upload Cancellation and Abort Logic
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a User, I want to cancel an upload if I select the wrong file so that I don't have to wait for a useless analysis to finish.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
Video files can be large. This implementation uses AbortController to save bandwidth and server resources.

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* Add a visible 'Cancel' button during the loading state.
* Trigger AbortController.abort() on press.
* Ensure WebSocket is closed and UI returns to initial state.

stories.summary: Optimization: Reduce Skeleton Latency via High-Frequency Polling
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a Hitter, I want the skeleton to track my movement in real-time so that I can accurately analyze my mechanics without visual lag.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
The default 500ms update interval for expo-av is insufficient for high-velocity sports analysis.

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* Set progressUpdateIntervalMillis to 16ms.
* Verify landmark synchronization at 60fps.
* Ensure no significant CPU overhead on older devices.

stories.summary: Optimization: Adjust Overlay UI for Safe Area Compliance
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a Hitter, I want the UI controls to be easily reachable so that I don't accidentally trigger system gestures while trying to minimize the video.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
The minimize button was positioned too low, interfering with the home indicator on iOS and Android.

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* Increase bottom margin for control buttons to minimum 24px.
* Implement conditional positioning for Fullscreen vs Card view.
* Verify tap success rate on devices with edge-to-edge displays.

stories.summary: Feature: Custom Fullscreen Analysis View
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a Hitter, I want to see the skeletal analysis in fullscreen so I can study the fine details of my movements without the skeleton disappearing.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
Native fullscreen obscures the SVG overlay. This implementation uses a layout-level expansion to preserve the skeleton.

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* Custom 'Full Screen' button implemented in the overlay.
* Uses conditional styling to expand the videoWrapper to fill the screen.
* Maintains SVG-to-Video sync during resize events.

stories.summary: Optimization: Migrate Video Engine to expo-video (fix_7)
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a Developer, I want to use the modern expo-video engine so that I can avoid deprecation warnings while maintaining sub-millisecond skeleton sync.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
Initial migration failed due to inconsistent timeUpdate events. Implementing explicit timeUpdateEventInterval to match 60fps tracking requirements.

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* Remove all expo-av dependencies and imports.
* Initialize player with timeUpdateEventInterval = 0.016.
* Verify 'Clock Pulse' logs appear in the terminal during playback.
* Ensure SkeletonOverlay aligns correctly in both Card and Fullscreen modes.

stories.summary: Optimization: SVG Coordinate Calibration
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a User, I want the skeletal overlay to align perfectly with my body in the video so that the analysis is visually accurate.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
Currently, the SVG overlay uses the container dimensions (videoWrapper), which includes letterboxing (black bars). We need to calculate the 'Active Video Area' and scale landmarks specifically to that area[cite: 57].

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* Dynamic Scaling: Update SkeletonOverlay to accept 'naturalSize' from the video player.
* Letterbox Handling: Calculate the X/Y offset for centered videos to prevent the 'floating' effect seen in the screenshot.
* Resize Stability: Ensure the skeleton stays aligned when switching between portrait and landscape videos.

h3. ⚙️ Technical Implementation Details
* Use `onReadyForDisplay` from `expo-av` to get `naturalSize`.
* Implement a mapping function: `targetX = (landmark.x * videoActualWidth) + horizontalOffset`.
* Ensure `SkeletonOverlay` styles use `pointerEvents='none'` to avoid blocking video controls.

h3. ⚠️ Edge Cases & Constraints
* Vertical Video: Ensure 9:16 'shorts' style videos don't stretch the skeleton horizontally.
* Cropped Videos: Handle videos where the aspect ratio is manually altered by the user before upload.

stories.summary: Feature: React Web Application Parity
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a User, I want to access DiamondMind via a web browser so that I can analyze and review my swings on a desktop or larger screen.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
While mobile is the primary capture tool, a web interface allows for deeper analysis and better accessibility. We will leverage the existing Vite/React setup on Vercel[cite: 25, 31, 55].

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* Environment: Configure the existing Vercel project to serve a responsive web UI alongside the mobile-focused views[cite: 29, 37].
* Analysis Parity: Port the video upload and WebSocket progress tracking logic from the mobile app to the web client[cite: 13, 48].
* Visualization: Implement the DM-30 skeletal overlay using web-compatible SVG libraries[cite: 57].
* Responsive Design: Ensure the layout adjusts for desktop, tablet, and mobile browsers.
* Authentication: (Future) Prepare for a shared login system so swings uploaded on mobile appear on the web.

h3. ⚙️ Technical Implementation Details
* Framework: React (Vite) with Tailwind CSS v4[cite: 57].
* API Integration: Continue using `axios` and `httpx` to communicate with the Render Backend[cite: 57, 58].
* Video Handling: Use standard HTML5 video tags or a React-specific wrapper for desktop playback parity with `expo-av`[cite: 57].

h3. ⚠️ Edge Cases & Constraints
* Browser Compatibility: Ensure WebSocket stability across Chrome, Safari, and Firefox.
* File Sizes: Desktop users may attempt to upload much larger raw video files than mobile users; enforce the 50MB limit at the browser level[cite: 53].
* Drag and Drop: Implement a desktop-friendly drag-and-drop zone for video files.

stories.summary: Feature: Skeletal Overlay UI Rendering
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a User, I want to see a skeletal overlay drawn over my swing video so that I can visually confirm the AI's tracking and analyze my body positions.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
Now that we have the landmark data and the video, we need to synchronize them and render a visual representation of the 33 MediaPipe points on the mobile UI.

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* Video Playback: Integrate `expo-av` to play the analyzed swing video.
* SVG Layer: Implement a `react-native-svg` overlay that sits perfectly on top of the video component.
* Coordinate Mapping: Scale the normalized (0.0 - 1.0) landmark coordinates to the actual pixel dimensions of the display.
* Bones/Joints: Draw lines (bones) connecting specific joint IDs (e.g., shoulder to elbow) and circles for the landmarks.
* Sync: Ensure the skeletal frame updates in real-time as the video plays back.
* Performance: The overlay must render smoothly without significant lag or jitter.

h3. ⚙️ Technical Implementation Details
* Frontend: React Native with `expo-av` for video and `react-native-svg` for rendering.
* Logic: Use a `useRef` to track video playback time and map it to the 'timestamp_ms' in the AI JSON results.
* Assets: Define a 'POSE_CONNECTIONS' constant that maps which landmark IDs should be connected by lines.

h3. ⚠️ Edge Cases & Constraints
* Aspect Ratio: Handle cases where the video aspect ratio (e.g., 9:16) differs from the phone screen container.
* Missing Data: Gracefully hide the skeleton if a specific frame has low visibility or missing landmarks.
* Seeking: Ensure the skeleton stays in sync if the user scrubs through the video timeline.

stories.summary: Optimization: Mobile-Side Resolution Scaling
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a User, I want the app to downscale my high-resolution videos before uploading so that I save data and reduce the time spent waiting for AI processing.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
High-res 4K/60fps files can exceed 100MB and overwhelm the free-tier AI Service memory (512MB RAM). Scaling to 720p maintains landmark accuracy while significantly improving stability.

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* Pre-processing: Integrate a compression step immediately after the video is selected from the gallery.
* Target Specs: Downscale to 720p (1280x720) with a maximum bitrate of 2.5 Mbps.
* UI Feedback: Show a 'Preparing Video...' or 'Optimizing...' status bar during the compression phase.
* Handover: The resulting compressed file must be passed to the existing UploadService logic seamlessly.
* Stability: Ensure the app doesn't crash during memory-intensive compression on older devices.

h3. ⚙️ Technical Implementation Details
* Library: `expo-video-compressor` or `react-native-compressor`.
* Workflow: Picker -> Compression -> Upload -> WebSocket Progress Tracking.
* Configuration: Use 'Medium' or '720p' preset to balance speed and landmark visibility.

h3. ⚠️ Edge Cases & Constraints
* Low Storage: Handle errors if the user's phone has no space to save the temporary compressed file.
* Ultra-short videos: Ensure the compressor doesn't break if a video is less than 1 second long.
* Already Small: Skip compression if the original file is already < 720p and under 10MB.

stories.summary: Optimization: AI Service Frame Skipping
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a Developer, I want the AI Engine to process every Nth frame so that analysis finishes 2x faster on CPU-limited free-tier hardware.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
Processing 60 frames per second is compute-heavy. For swing analysis, 30fps provides sufficient data points for skeletal rendering while cutting processing time in half.

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* Engine Logic: Update the `while cap.isOpened()` loop in `pose_engine.py` to skip frames based on a configurable variable.
* Consistency: Ensure the `timestamp_ms` passed to MediaPipe correctly matches the actual video time of the frame being processed.
* WebSocket Accuracy: The progress bar must still calculate percentage based on (current_frame / total_video_frames) even when skipping.
* Speed: Aim for a 40-50% reduction in end-to-end processing time on Render Free Tier.

h3. ⚙️ Technical Implementation Details
* Logic: Use `if frame_count % 2 != 0: continue` for a quick 50% skip rate.
* OpenCV: Alternatively, use `cap.set(cv2.CAP_PROP_POS_FRAMES, ...)` to seek forward for higher efficiency.
* AI Output: The resulting JSON must still represent a continuous (though lower frequency) timeline of the swing.

h3. ⚠️ Edge Cases & Constraints
* High-Speed Video: If a user uploads 120fps or 240fps slow-mo, the skipping logic should potentially scale (e.g., skip every 4 frames).
* Last Frame: Ensure the very last frame of the video is still processed to avoid 'cutoff' data in the UI.
* Metadata mismatch: Ensure `total_frames` in the success JSON reflects the frames *processed*, not just the raw video count.

stories.summary: Feature: Real-Time Analysis Progress via WebSockets
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a User, I want to see a real-time progress bar during analysis so that I know exactly how much of my video has been processed.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
Current HTTP implementation is a 'black box' until completion. We need a persistent connection to stream frame-by-frame progress from the AI Engine to the Mobile UI.

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* Backend: Implement a WebSocket endpoint `/ws/analysis/{job_id}` using FastAPI.
* AI Service: Update the processing loop to emit a 'progress_update' event after every 5-10 frames.
* Mobile: Replace the static spinner with a percentage-based progress bar (0-100%).
* Reliability: Handle WebSocket disconnection/reconnection if the signal drops mid-swing.
* Cleanup: Ensure WebSocket connections are closed once the final JSON result is delivered.

h3. ⚙️ Technical Implementation Details
* Protocol: WebSockets (WSS).
* Backend: FastAPI `WebsocketManager` to track active client connections.
* Frontend: React Native `WebSocket` API integrated into the Analysis screen.

stories.summary: Feature: Video Upload Gateway & AI Orchestration
stories.description:
{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
*User Story*

As a User, I want to upload my swing video to the main Backend so that it can be stored and sent to the AI Service for analysis without timing out.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal

The Main Backend (Render) acts as the secure orchestrator. It must handle incoming multi-part video streams and forward them to the Dockerized AI Service. Because video processing is heavy, we must manage timeouts and file size limits specifically.

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)

* Endpoint `POST /api/videos/upload` is active on the Main Backend.
* Backend pulls `AI_SERVICE_URL` from environment variables for flexible routing.
* The service uses `httpx.AsyncClient` with a minimum 60-second timeout to allow for AI processing time.
* Successfully forwards the `UploadFile` stream without loading the entire video into RAM (memory efficiency).
* Returns a standardized error JSON if the AI Service is unreachable or returns a 5xx error.

h3. ⚙️ Technical Implementation Details

* Request Flow: Client (Vite) -> Backend (FastAPI) -> AI Service (Docker/MediaPipe).
* Timeout Config: Set `httpx` timeout to 120.0s to prevent 'Gateway Timeout' during heavy analysis.
* Payload Limit: Restrict uploads to 50MB at the FastAPI level to prevent server exhaustion.
* CORS: Ensure the Backend allows `POST` and `OPTIONS` from the Vercel production domain.

h3. ⚠️ Edge Cases & Constraints

* AI Service Cold Start: Handle the delay if the AI Service is 'sleeping' on the Render Free tier.
* Interrupted Upload: Ensure temp files are cleaned up if a user closes the browser mid-upload.
* Unsupported Formats: Validate that the file is an `.mp4`, `.mov`, or `.avi` before forwarding to the AI service.
* Network Jitter: Implement a 'retry' logic (optional) if the internal connection between Render services blips.

stories.summary: Feature: Dockerize AI Service for Cloud Deployment
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a DevOps Engineer, I want to containerize the AI Service using Docker so that it can run reliably on Render (or any cloud provider) with all system-level dependencies pre-installed.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
The AI Service relies on OpenCV (`cv2`) and MediaPipe. These libraries require system-level shared objects (like `libGL` and `libglib`) that are missing in standard 'Python Native' cloud environments. A Docker container is the only way to bundle these OS dependencies.

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* A `Dockerfile` is created in the `ai-service/` directory.
* The Docker build process successfully installs Python 3.12, system dependencies (`libgl1`, `libglib2.0`), and Python packages.
* The `.task` model file is correctly copied into the container image.
* The container exposes port 8001 and starts the FastAPI server (`uvicorn`) automatically.
* Local testing (`docker run`) confirms the service responds to health checks.

h3. ⚙️ Technical Implementation Details
* Base Image: `python:3.12-slim` (to keep size down).
* System Deps: Run `apt-get install -y libgl1-mesa-glx libglib2.0-0` before `pip install`.
* Command: `CMD ["python", "main.py"]` or `uvicorn` entrypoint.
* Port Mapping: Ensure internal port 8001 maps correctly to the host.

h3. ⚠️ Edge Cases & Constraints
* Model File Missing: Ensure the `.dockerignore` file doesn't accidentally exclude the `.task` file.
* Memory Limits: MediaPipe can be RAM hungry; ensure the container isn't immediately OOM (Out of Memory) killed on free-tier hosting.
* Architecture: Ensure the image builds correctly for Linux (amd64) even if developed on Apple Silicon (arm64).

stories.summary: Feature: Video Upload API & Stream Handling
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a User, I want to upload a raw video file via the web interface, so that the system can receive and store it for processing without manual file access.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
The AI engine (DM-12) works on local files. We need a bridge to accept 'multipart/form-data' from the frontend, save it to a temp directory, and feed it to the engine.

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* API endpoint (POST /analyze/upload) accepts 'multipart/form-data' (binary video stream).
* Server saves the incoming stream to a temporary storage location with a unique ID.
* Server validates file type (must be .mp4, .mov) and rejects non-video files.
* API passes the temp file path to the DM-12 AI Engine for processing.
* System cleans up (deletes) the temporary file after analysis is complete/returned.

h3. ⚙️ Technical Implementation Details
* Framework: FastAPI 'UploadFile'.
* Library: 'shutil' for file saving.
* Storage: Local 'temp/' directory (ensure it exists and is gitignored).

h3. ⚠️ Edge Cases & Constraints
* Large Files: Set a hard limit (e.g., 50MB) to prevent server memory crashes.
* Concurrent Uploads: Ensure unique filenames (UUIDs) so two users don't overwrite each other's video.
* Cleanup Failure: If the app crashes during analysis, ensure old temp files are eventually purged.

stories.summary: Feature: Integrated Video Import & Cloud Analysis
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a User, I want to select a video from my camera roll so that I can analyze my previous swings using the DiamondMind AI engine.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
This is the primary data entry point. We need to bridge the mobile device's file system with our Render-hosted Backend Orchestrator.

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* UI: Add an 'Upload Swing' button to the mobile dashboard using Lucide-React icons.
* Picker: Trigger `expo-image-picker` to open the native iOS/Android video gallery.
* Validation: Prevent uploads of files >50MB or non-video formats.
* Transmission: Upload the file as `multipart/form-data` to the Main Backend URL.
* User Feedback: Display a 'Processing...' loading state while the 120s AI timeout is active.
* Success: Display the resulting landmark JSON (or a 'Success' message) in the mobile UI.

h3. ⚙️ Technical Implementation Details
* Frontend: React Native (Expo) + Tailwind (NativeWind).
* API Client: `axios` configured with a 120,000ms timeout.
* Permissions: Ensure `app.json` includes 'Camera Roll' permissions for iOS/Android.

h3. ⚠️ Edge Cases & Constraints
* iPhone HEVC: If the device uses High Efficiency (H.265), ensure the picker allows the OS to handle standard format export.
* Network Switch: Handle cases where the user moves from Wi-Fi to LTE mid-upload.
* Long Processing: Ensure the phone screen doesn't go to sleep while waiting for the AI response.

stories.summary: Feature: Pitching Analysis Mode
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a Pitcher, I want to analyze my pitching mechanics so I can improve my delivery and prevent injury.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
Different biomechanics than hitting. Needs a separate 'Mode' in the UI and different heuristics for the AI.

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* UI toggle to switch between 'Hitting' and 'Pitching' modes.
* AI evaluates specific pitching metrics: Stride Length, Arm Slot, Release Point.
* Distinct System Prompt for pitching feedback.

h3. ⚙️ Technical Implementation Details
* Reuse DM-12 (Skeleton Extraction).
* New heuristic analysis module: `analyze_pitching(landmarks)`.

h3. ⚠️ Edge Cases & Constraints
* Camera Angle: Pitching is often filmed from behind the mound (Hitting is side view). AI must detect or ask for angle.
* Lefties: Ensure arm slot analysis isn't inverted for left-handed pitchers.

stories.summary: Feature: User Profile System
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a User, I want to create a profile with my age and height so that the AI can calibrate its analysis for me.
{panel}

* User can sign up/login (Auth).

stories.summary: Feature: Text-to-Speech Feedback
stories.description:

As a Player practicing alone, I want to hear the coaching feedback via audio so I don't have to look at the screen between swings.

stories.summary: Feature: Visual Stick-Figure Overlay
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a Coach, I want to see a stick-figure skeleton overlaid on the video so that I can visually verify body positions.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
Visual validation of DM-12. We need to draw lines connecting the extracted coordinate points on top of the video player.

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* Video player renders SVG or Canvas layer on top of video.
* Skeleton lines connect correct joints (e.g., shoulder to elbow, elbow to wrist).
* Overlay stays synchronized with video playback.
* User can toggle overlay ON/OFF.

h3. ⚙️ Technical Implementation Details
* Frontend: React Native Skia or SVG.
* Logic: Map normalized (0-1) coordinates from DM-12 JSON to screen pixel dimensions.

h3. ⚠️ Edge Cases & Constraints
* Aspect Ratio Mismatch: Ensure lines align correctly even if video is cropped or scaled.
* Missing Data: Handle frames where DM-12 returned 'null' for a joint (don't draw random lines to 0,0).

stories.summary: Feature: AI Skeleton Extraction Engine (Core)
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a System, I want to extract skeletal coordinates from a local video file path, so that raw biomechanical data is available for analysis.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
This is the core engine of DiamondMind. We need to ingest raw video footage and output a structured time-series of skeletal coordinates. This data will power the Stick-Figure Overlay and Swing Analysis.

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* System accepts a local file path (string) as input.
* System extracts 33 key body landmarks using MediaPipe Tasks 'Heavy' model.
* Output is a standardized JSON time-series (frame_idx, timestamp, x, y, z, visibility).
* Processing handles occlusion and low-confidence frames gracefully.
* Engine is decoupled from HTTP upload logic (pure processing unit).

h3. ⚙️ Technical Implementation Details
* Model: MediaPipe Pose Landmarker (Tasks API).
* Input: Video File Path (String).
* Output: JSON Schema with frame_index, timestamp_ms, and landmarks.
* Language: Python 3.12+.

h3. ⚠️ Edge Cases & Constraints
* Occlusion: The bat crossing the body or the camera angle hiding the back arm.
* Motion Blur: Fast bat speeds blurring the hands.
* Multiple People: Ensure the model tracks the *primary* subject (the batter) if other players are in the background.

stories.summary: Feature: Delete Swing History
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a User, I want to delete old or accidental swing uploads so that I can keep my library clean.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
Users need control over their data. This requires a destructive action that removes the record from the DB and the associated video file from storage.

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* UI provides a 'Delete' button on the Swing Detail view.
* User is prompted with a confirmation modal before deletion.
* Backend removes the database row AND the associated video file from cloud storage.
* List view automatically refreshes to remove the deleted item.

h3. ⚙️ Technical Implementation Details
* Endpoint: DELETE /swings/{id}
* Storage: Ensure cloud storage deletion (e.g., S3/Supabase Storage delete call).

h3. ⚠️ Edge Cases & Constraints
* Orphaned Files: If DB delete succeeds but Storage delete fails, log an error for cleanup.
* Concurrency: User tries to delete a file while it is currently being analyzed.

stories.summary: Centralized Cloud Database for Persistent Storage
stories.description:
{panel:title=User Story|bgColor=#EAE6FF}
As a Developer, I need a centralized cloud database to store user data and swing analysis results so that data persists across sessions and devices.
{panel}

h3. 🧠 Context & Goal
Implemented PostgreSQL database integration using Render's managed PostgreSQL service. The system now supports persistent storage with a three-table schema (Users, Swings, Analysis Results) with proper foreign key relationships and cascading deletes. SQLAlchemy ORM provides the data access layer, and Alembic handles database migrations.

h3. ✅ Acceptance Criteria (Definition of Done)
* âœ… PostgreSQL instance provisioned and accessible via connection string (Render PostgreSQL)
* âœ… Schema migration scripts created for tables: 'users', 'swings', 'analysis_results'
* âœ… Backend can successfully read/write to the database
* âœ… Environment variables for DB credentials are secured in .env
* âœ… CRUD endpoints implemented for users and swings
* âœ… Video upload pipeline saves results to database
* âœ… All tests passing (user creation, swing creation, analysis storage, cascading deletes)

h3. ⚙️ Technical Implementation Details
* Database Provider: Render PostgreSQL (Internal networking for better performance)
* 
* Schema Design:
* - users: id, email (unique), username (unique), created_at, updated_at
* - swings: id, user_id (FKâ†’users), filename, video_url, created_at
* - analysis_results: id, swing_id (FKâ†’swings), skeletal_data (JSONB), total_frames, frames_with_person, fps, bat_trail (JSONB), phase, score, feedback, drill, drill_explanation, created_at
* 
* Implementation:
* - database.py: PostgreSQL connection pooling (pool_pre_ping=True, pool_size=5, max_overflow=10)
* - models.py: SQLAlchemy ORM models with relationships and cascading deletes
* - Alembic: Migration framework for version-controlled schema changes
* - main.py: Startup event creates tables, CRUD endpoints, database persistence in upload pipeline
* 
* New Endpoints:
* - POST /api/users - Create user
* - GET /api/users/{user_id} - Get user details
* - GET /api/users/{user_id}/swings - Get user's swings
* - GET /api/swings/{swing_id}/analysis - Get swing analysis
* 
* Upload Enhancement:
* - /api/videos/upload now accepts optional user_id parameter
* - Background processor saves Swing and AnalysisResult to database
* - Returns swing_id and analysis_id in WebSocket response
* 
* Local Development:
* - SQLite fallback when DATABASE_URL not set
* - Tables auto-created on startup via Base.metadata.create_all()
* - test_database.py validates all CRUD operations
* 
* Production Deployment:
* - DATABASE_URL environment variable (use Render Internal URL)
* - Connection pooling handles cold starts
* - JSONB columns in PostgreSQL for efficient JSON storage

h3. ⚠️ Edge Cases & Constraints
* âœ… Connection Timeout: pool_pre_ping=True verifies connections before use, handles DB cold starts
* âœ… Data Integrity: Foreign keys with ON DELETE CASCADE configured (deleting user deletes all swings and analysis)
* âœ… Backward Compatibility: user_id is optional in upload endpoint, works without database
* âœ… Local Development: SQLite fallback allows development without cloud database
* âœ… Migration Conflicts: Alembic tracks schema versions to prevent conflicts
* Database Size Limits: Render free tier has 1GB storage, 30-day expiration (Starter tier $7/month recommended for production)
* Concurrent Writes: PostgreSQL handles concurrent inserts, connection pooling prevents connection exhaustion
* JSON Data Size: skeletal_data and bat_trail stored as JSONB, indexed for efficient queries

stories.summary: Feature: Display Timestamps in History
stories.description: As a user, I want to see WHEN I took the swing (e.g., 'Dec 23, 10:30 AM') so I can differentiate sessions.
